text: Carl Olof Trygg (December 21, 1910 – 1993) was one of the recognized masters of 20th century woodcarving, renowned for the Scandinavian flat-plane style. Born in Stora Tuna, Kopparberg county, Dalarna, Sweden, he was one of three sons of Carl Johan Trygg and Maria Axelina Andersson. Carl Olof worked with his father carving wooden figures of common people in the Scandinavian flat-plane style. Together with his father Carl Johan and two brothers, Nils and Lars, they produced over 10,000 carvings. Many of these figures were sold to tourists for approximately US$10.00; adjusted for inflation, that amount would be equivalent to $108.05 in 2005. At age 17, Carl Olof immigrated to Canada with his mother Maria (43), brother Nils Johan (13), and an unknown relative, possibly his sister Kally Maria Trygg (8), arriving in Halifax, Nova Scotia on October 7, 1928. His father Carl Johan had arrived in Halifax on March 3, 1928. The family eventually settled in Montreal, Quebec, where they continued carving. Between Carl Johan Trygg and his sons, over 10,000 figures were carved. Trygg was a craftsman aligned with the tourist trade, typically creating solo figures from basswood or pine, mounted on a base, with clean cuts and a stylized execution from a single piece of wood. A notable feature of his work is the use of vibrant paint, often applied to clothing in plaid patterns. Carl Johan Trygg and Carl Olof Trygg later returned to Sweden, where they continued their careers; Carl Johan died there in 1954, and Carl Olof was producing figures as late as 1987. Trygg family woodcarvings remain highly sought after as collectibles, with over 10,000 figures produced by family members, priced between $50 and $500 based on age, size, and condition. The carvings can be identified by signatures and dates on the bases, with common signatures including the carver’s name and year, such as "C.O. Trygg 1961 Sweden," indicating the piece was carved by Carl Olof Trygg in 1961 while living in Sweden.
